gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-parkinsans: Crisp, wide-mouthed letters carry the text, and Blockletter above them stands tall in the middle, drawn like pencil that never presses harder. Parkinsans holds one stroke thickness throughout, so a full page moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-pathway-extrem: Blockletter skims along with a stroke weight that never changes, its tall midsection like a squat brush-pen belly. Pathway Extreme adds stubby ascenders and clear openings, and Blockletter earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-preahvihear: Pencil-sketched and precise, Blockletter hands off to Preahvihear, whose open mouths and lofty x-height resemble pried oysters. Blockletter's unchanging one-weight stroke is what makes this pairing stick in the mind.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-pt-sans-captio: PT Sans Caption has big-bodied lowercase and bowls left inviting and unclosed. PT Sans Caption sits under Blockletter, whose look comes from a single cutting width, like a laser-cut sheet.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-puritan: Puritan keeps its rounded forms clearly open to the side, with oversized counters in the e and a. But Blockletter, cut at a single depth like an engraving, wants room, so give it the bigger size.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-questrial: Questrial reads flat and stencil-cut, its single-weight strokes forming a tall band of letters with short stalks above. Beside Blockletter's brush-pen belly, pages of text would feel smooth and unhurried.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada stands tall and full in its lowercase c, s and z. Beneath Blockletter's pencil-sketched headings, a steady line with no pressure shifts and open curve endings keep paragraphs moving comfortably.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-radio-canada-b: Brush-pen belly, pencil-sketched line, all of it Blockletter and all of it precise. Radio Canada Big takes over below, a monoline skeleton with an x-height filling the line and terminals finishing away from the stem.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-readex-pro: A tall midsection like a squat brush-pen belly marks Blockletter, while Readex Pro opens broad gaps at its terminals. Their shared, unvarying line weight is the quiet strength here.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-roboto: Precise and modern, Blockletter looks like a bent paperclip. Roboto opens generous mouths on its round letters and keeps capitals close to lowercase height, so paragraphs go down without a snag.
